References / Editorial / 91

“Ist diese Typografie noch zu retten?”,
TM special issue

The December 1976 special issue of Typografische Monatsblätter on Weingart’s work from 1969 to 1976, with banded bilingual text on the cover and dense film collages inside.

Source
Letterform Archive: Legacies of Swiss Style, Part 2—Wolfgang Weingart
Creator
Wolfgang Weingart
Made
December 1976 (Letterform Archive)
Style
New Wave typography (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Kinetic, rebellious, layered, experimental
Evidence
Inspected Letterform Archive’s photograph of the cover and one interior spread of the Archive’s copy (3000 × 1304) in a scratchpad copy. Not stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Letterform Archive says the issue was produced under Weingart’s supervision and marks the end of his early years on the TM editorial board. It shows seven years of his work in collages of image and text, with “spaced-out letterforms, misaligned images, thick black text boxes, and a broken grid”. Letterform Archive.

The compositions were made by layering photographic films, not on a computer. Letterform Archive.

The cover asks “Is This Typography Worth Supporting, Or Do We Live On The Moon?” and calls the issue “a special selection from the works of Weingart, from 1969–1976”.

Observed

  • The cover is light grey with a masthead of thick and thin rules that divides the three journal names into cells.
  • The heading is bold grotesque. The subtitle lines are white on black bars that change length from line to line.
  • Body text alternates bold German lines and regular English lines. Each line sits on a grey or white band, and some lines are struck through by horizontal rules.
  • Four-digit numbers (0001, 0094) mark the lines in the left margin in two weights.
  • The interior spread is a black-and-white collage: halftone portraits, fragments of a New York street map with zip codes on diagonal bands, stars, Swiss crosses, diagonal stripes, a grid of numbered cells, and a small arrow-shaped caption box.

Why it belongs

The cover turns reading order into structure: bands, strikes, and line numbers show the alternation of two languages. The collage shows how far the style goes when type is only one layer among many.

Borrow

Put alternate lines of a bilingual text on bands of two different tints.

Number lines in the margin in a small bold grotesque.

Use a map fragment on a diagonal band as a texture layer behind photographs.
